title: Biting Frost Support Guide — Tiers, Freeze Consumption and Valid Skills
summary: Biting Frost is a Support Gem family (I / II / III) for Cold skills. Socketed into a Cold Hit, it makes that Hit Consume Freeze on the enemy to deal extra Cold Damage. The target must already be Frozen, and the Freeze is consumed by the hit. It shines on packs and Frozen rares, and is weaker on bosses that resist Freeze.
description: Biting Frost Support deep guide: what Biting Frost I / II / III each are, when you get each tier, Hit-only and Frozen-required rules, Freeze consumption and the damage bonus, normal vs Rare vs Unique behaviour, Herald of Ice and Glacial Cascade conflicts, the valid-skill matrix, and why Socket Compatible is not the same as recommended.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial
imageAlt: Biting Frost cold support gem icon

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: Biting Frost is a Support Gem family with three tiers: Biting Frost I, II and III, obtained at different gemcutting levels. All three do the same thing mechanically — they make a supported Cold Hit Consume Freeze on the enemy for extra Cold Damage.
The supported skill must be a Hit, and the enemy must already be Frozen. The Hit consumes the Freeze to grant a damage bonus; if the enemy is not Frozen, Biting Frost does nothing extra.
It is great on Frozen packs and rares, and weak on bosses that resist Freeze. 'Socket Compatible' only means the gem fits; it does not mean the support is worth using on that skill.

supports.label: Biting Frost I
notes: Base tier, obtained early from an Uncut Support Gem.
Supported Cold Hits Consume Freeze for a small extra Cold Damage bonus.

supports.label: Biting Frost II
notes: Higher gemcutting tier; larger Freeze-consumption Cold Damage bonus.
Same rule: Hit must be Cold and target must be Frozen.

supports.label: Biting Frost III
notes: Top tier; strongest Freeze-consumption Cold Damage bonus.
Use this when available; lower tiers are direct upgrades of the same effect.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: The supported skill must deal Cold Damage and must be a Hit. Damage-over-time or non-Cold skills gain nothing from Biting Frost.
The enemy must be in the Frozen state when the Hit lands. Biting Frost does not apply Freeze; something else must Freeze the enemy first.

keyValues.label: Cold Hit
notes: Only Cold damage hits can Consume Freeze via this support.

keyValues.label: Target Frozen
notes: Biting Frost consumes an existing Freeze; it does not create one.

sections.title: Freeze Consumption
paragraphs: When a supported Cold Hit lands on a Frozen enemy, Biting Frost Consumes the Freeze and grants extra Cold Damage on that Hit. The Freeze is removed by the consumption, so the enemy is no longer Frozen after the hit.

The bonus applies per Hit. If a skill has several hit parts (a main projectile plus shards, for example), each Frozen-hitting part can Consume Freeze separately, as long as the enemy is still Frozen when that part lands.
Because the Freeze is consumed, you need a way to re-Freeze (or a source of frequent Freezes) to keep getting the bonus on the same enemy.
bullets: Hit on Frozen enemy → Consume Freeze → extra Cold Damage.
Each Cold hit part can consume if the enemy is still Frozen.

sections.title: Valid Skill Matrix
rows: Main hit; consumes Freeze for bonus damage
Separate hit parts; each can consume if still Frozen
Herald is not a Biting Frost-supported hit; no consumption
Payoff segment benefits from Freeze consumption
Multiple Freeze consumers can compete for the same Freeze

sections.title: Normal, Rare and Unique Rules
paragraphs: Normal enemies Freeze easily, so Biting Frost pays off constantly on packs. Rares have higher ailment thresholds but still Freeze often enough to be worth it.

Uniques and bosses resist Freeze (high ailment threshold), so they are rarely Frozen long enough for Biting Frost to consume. On bosses the support contributes little unless you invest heavily in Freeze application or the boss is susceptible.
The damage bonus itself does not change by enemy type; the difference is simply how often the enemy is Frozen and therefore how often the bonus can apply.
bullets: Rares: usually Freeze, usually worth it.
Bosses / Uniques: rare Freeze, rarely worth it.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Biting Frost stacks with other Cold damage supports (Cold Penetration, Elemental Damage, Cold Mastery-style supports) because it only adds to the Hit's Cold Damage when a Freeze is consumed.
It competes with other Freeze consumers on the same skill. If a skill already Consumes Freeze for its own effect (like Glacial Cascade), adding Biting Frost means they fight over the same Freeze.

keyValues.label: Cold Damage / Penetration
notes: Scale the Cold Damage that Biting Frost adds on consumption.

keyValues.label: Freeze application supports
notes: More Freeze uptime means more chances to consume.

keyValues.label: Other Freeze consumers
notes: Glacial Cascade etc. compete for the same Freeze.

sections.title: Skill Interactions
paragraphs: Herald of Ice: its explosion is not a Biting Frost-supported hit, so Biting Frost does not add to Herald of Ice shatters. They can coexist, but Biting Frost does not boost the Herald.
Freezing Mark: a strong enabler — it helps apply Freeze so your Biting Frost hits have something to consume.
Glacial Cascade: also Consumes Freeze; socketing both on the same skill means they compete for the Freeze rather than stacking cleanly.
bullets: Herald of Ice: not boosted by Biting Frost.
Freezing Mark: enables more Freeze to consume.

sections.title: Mapping Usage
paragraphs: In maps, packs Freeze easily and die fast, so Biting Frost pays off on almost every Cold Hit. This is its best environment.

steps.label: Freeze the pack
steps.action: Apply Freeze with your Cold skill or Freezing Mark.
steps.result: Enemies are in a consumable state.

steps.label: Consume on hit
steps.result: Extra Cold Damage per Frozen hit; rapid clear.

sections.title: Bossing Usage
paragraphs: On bosses that resist Freeze, Biting Frost rarely has a Freeze to consume, so its value drops sharply. Keep it only if your build applies Freeze reliably to the boss, or swap it for a plain Cold damage support.

steps.label: Can you Freeze the boss?
steps.result: If yes, Biting Frost still helps; if no, swap it.

sections.title: Build Usage
paragraphs: Ice Shot Deadeye: a Cold bow build where Biting Frost adds damage whenever Frozen enemies are hit by the arrow and shards.
Cold Caster Chronomancer: a Cold spell shell that uses Freeze-heavy skills, making Biting Frost a natural damage support.
Any Freeze-focused Cold build: if you Freeze often, Biting Frost converts that Freeze into direct damage.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No bonus damage: the enemy was not Frozen when the Hit landed. Direct answer: Freeze first, then hit; Biting Frost does not apply Freeze.
Bonus stopped after one hit: the Freeze was consumed. Direct answer: re-Freeze to get more bonuses on the same enemy.
Boss barely benefits: bosses resist Freeze. Direct answer: swap Biting Frost for a flat Cold damage support on bosses.
Gem fits but feels weak: Socket Compatible is not a recommendation. Direct answer: judge by how often you actually Freeze, not by socket compatibility.

steps.label: No bonus
steps.result: Biting Frost can consume the Freeze.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Players note that the old single 'Biting Frost' name migrated into the I / II / III family, and the higher tiers are direct upgrades of the same effect.
The most common mistake is assuming Biting Frost applies Freeze; it only consumes one. Builds that forget to Freeze see no bonus.
The Glacial Cascade overlap is a known point of confusion: two Freeze consumers on one skill compete rather than stack.
bullets: Recurring note: old name is now I / II / III tiers.
Recurring mistake: Biting Frost does not apply Freeze.
Known conflict: Glacial Cascade also consumes Freeze.
